MFA.CROB No. 37 of 2019

THESE APPEALS & MFA CROB ARE COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Aggrieved by the common judgment passed in MVC Nos.728/2015 and 790/2015, two appellants are before this court in MFA No.5621/2018 and 6848/2018.
In MFA No.5621/2018, a cross objection is filed in MFA Crob. No.37/2019 by the claimants.

2. It is the case of the claimants that on 02.06.2015 at about 12.30 p.m., when the deceased in MVC No.790/2018 i.e., rider of the bike along with the pillion rider i.e., deceased in MVC No.728/2015,
were riding the motorbike at that point of time the driver of the KSRTC Bus drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and hit the bike.
Resultantly the rider of the bike died on the spot and the pillion rider succumbed to the injuries, later died in the hospital.

NC: 2023:KHC:41467 REGARDING LIABILITY:
3.
Claim petitions were filed claiming compensation of an amount of Rs.18,60,000/- in MVC No.728/2015, an amount of Rs.50,00,000/- in MVC No.790/2015 for the death of the deceased.
As per the claimants the rider of the vehicle was working as a coolie and earning an amount of Rs.25,000/- p.m., and there are three claimants.
As per the claimants of the pillion rider he was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The court below awarded an amount of Rs.7,85,000/- and an amount of Rs.3,44,500/- in MVC Nos.728/2015 and in MVC No.790/2015 respectively.

The court below on the question of liability, held that as the accident had taken place in the middle of the road and it is a case of 'head on collusion' there is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased rider and apportioned the contributory negligence at 50% on the rider and 50% on the driver of the KSRTC and exonerated the insurance company.

The claim petition against the insurance company which Smt Manjula vs Sri.Kumar P K on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22938228/
6 insured the bike was NC: 2023:KHC:41467 dismissed.

sentences.text: The liability was fixed on the KSRTC.
When it comes to the pillion rider an amount of Rs.8,35,000/- was awarded against the claimed amount of Rs.50,00,000/- and held that the KSRTC is liable to pay the compensation.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the KSRTC submits that when the court below has held that there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the bike and the driver of the KSRTC, in respect of the rider of the vehicle the court has apportioned the contributory negligence at 50% on both the vehicles i.e., owner of the bike as well as the driver of the KRSTC bus.

When it comes to the case of the pillion rider, the same analogy will apply and the court below ought to have apportioned the compensation amount on the insurer of the bike as well as the KSRTC, but the court below had only directed the KSRTC to pay the entire compensation which is bad in law.

Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company which in such the bike submits that the court below had rightly held that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation and it is the KSRTC which is liable to pay the compensation.
It is submitted that there are no grounds made out for interference with the award passed by the court below.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the rider of the bike submits that the court below went wrong in apportioning the contributory negligence.
It is submitted that when no evidence is let in by the insurance company , the court below ought not to have held that there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the vehicle.
It is submitted that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is without any basis and the amount that is taken by the court below as monthly income was on the lower side.
It is submitted that on other conventional heads also the amounts that were granted by the Tribunal are not reasonable.

Learned counsel appearing for the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:41467 pillion rider submits that the court below had granted a very meager amounts as compensation and it is submitted that taking the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000 p.m., was on the lower side.
7. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
In the background of the discussion above, first coming to the aspect of the liability.

In this case, the accident had taken place in the middle of the road and it is 'head on collusion' the court below had rightly come to the conclusion that there is a contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the bike and the driver of the KSRTC and apportioned the same at 50% on both the vehicles.
Then coming to the case of pillion rider, wherein the court below had directed the KSRTC to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the KSRTC when there is already apportionment of contributory negligence that there is negligence on the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41467 part of the rider of the bike, when both KSRTC as well as the insurer of bike are made parties and the pillion rider has chosen to initiate claim against both KSRTC as well as the insurer of the bike, the court below ought to have held both the insurer of the bike and KSRTC liable to pay 50% by apportioning the liability at 50%.
In view of the same as far as MFA No.6848/2018 is concerned the liability is rightly fixed by the Tribunal.
Whereas in MFA No.5621/2018 is concerned the insurance company of the bike shall pay 50% of the compensation amount and 50% shall be paid by the KSRTC.

REGARDING QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
I. MFA NO.6848/2018 IN MVC NO.790/2015:
9.
Now coming to the quantum of the compensation.
In respect of the rider of the vehicle the court below had considered the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/-, which is on lower side.
Considering the fact that this accident is of the year 2015, this Court is inclined to take monthly income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- as - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:41467 income.
The age of the rider of the vehicle is 46 years, 25% future prospects has to be added i.e., Rs.2,250/-.
Therefore, the income would be Rs.11,250/-p.m., as there are three dependants 1/3rd has to be deduced towards personal expenses then it would come to Rs.3,750/-.
His contribution to the family is 7500 i.e., 7500 x 12 x 13.
Hence, the loss of dependency to the family would be Rs.11,70,000/-.

As there are three dependants i.e., two sons and a wife towards loss of consortium the claimants are entitled for an amount of Rs.1,32,000/- (3 x 44,000), towards funeral expenses they are entitled for an amount of Rs.33,000/- is granted.

10. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards Legal Expenses.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Resultantly the rider of the bike died on the spot and the pillion rider succumbed to the injuries, later died in the hospital.
Claim petitions were filed claiming compensation of an amount of Rs.18,60,000/- in MVC No.728/2015, an amount of Rs.50,00,000/- in MVC No.790/2015 for the death of the deceased.
As per the claimants the rider of the vehicle was working as a coolie and earning an amount of Rs.25,000/- p.m., and there are three claimants.
As per the claimants of the pillion rider he was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The court below on the question of liability, held that as the accident had taken place in the middle of the road and it is a case of 'head on collusion' there is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased rider and apportioned the contributory negligence at 50% on the rider and 50% on the driver of the KSRTC and exonerated the insurance company.
The claim petition against the insurance company which Smt Manjula vs Sri.Kumar P K on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22938228/
6 insured the bike was NC: 2023:KHC:41467 dismissed.
The liability was fixed on the KSRTC.
When it comes to the pillion rider an amount of Rs.8,35,000/- was awarded against the claimed amount of Rs.50,00,000/- and held that the KSRTC is liable to pay the compensation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In this case, the accident had taken place in the middle of the road and it is 'head on collusion' the court below had rightly come to the conclusion that there is a contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the bike and the driver of the KSRTC and apportioned the same at 50% on both the vehicles.
Then coming to the case of pillion rider, wherein the court below had directed the KSRTC to pay the compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments: As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the KSRTC when there is already apportionment of contributory negligence that there is negligence on the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:41467 part of the rider of the bike, when both KSRTC as well as the insurer of bike are made parties and the pillion rider has chosen to initiate claim against both KSRTC as well as the insurer of the bike, the court below ought to have held both the insurer of the bike and KSRTC liable to pay 50% by apportioning the liability at 50%.
